revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Captain Vega's Four Clues
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega's expanded treasure map uses base camp at the origin (0, 0). Her four clues are at A(4, 3), B(-5, 2), C(-3, -4), and D(2, -5), where the x-coordinate is units east (+) or west (-) and the y-coordinate is units north (+) or south (-). Question: In which quadrant does each clue land, and how do the signs of its coordinates tell you that without plotting?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: A(4, 3) is in Quadrant I because both coordinates are positive (+, +) — east and north. B(-5, 2) is in Quadrant II because x is negative and y is positive (-, +) — west and north. C(-3, -4) is in Quadrant III because both are negative (-, -) — west and south. D(2, -5) is in Quadrant IV because x is positive and y is negative (+, -) — east and south.

questions.stem: In which quadrant is the point (-4, 5)?
questions.explanation: The x-coordinate is negative (left) and the y-coordinate is positive (up). Left and up is Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant III holds points where both coordinates are negative. Here the y-coordinate is 5, which is positive.
Quadrant IV pairs a positive x with a negative y. Look again at the sign of the x-coordinate in (-4, 5).
hints: Look at the signs: x = -4 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means move LEFT; positive y means move UP. Ask which corner of the plane is left-and-up.
From the origin, slide left 4 and climb up 5. Quadrants count I, II, III, IV counterclockwise from top-right.
questions.explanationEs: La coordenada x es negativa (izquierda) y la coordenada y es positiva (arriba). Izquierda y arriba es el cuadrante II.
hintsEs: Mira los signos: x = −4 es negativo y y = 5 es positivo.
Una x negativa significa moverse a la IZQUIERDA; una y positiva significa moverse hacia ARRIBA. Pregunta qué esquina del plano es izquierda y arriba.
Desde el origen, deslízate 4 a la izquierda y sube 5. Los cuadrantes se cuentan I, II, III, IV en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.

questions.stem: A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
questions.explanation: Positive x (right) and negative y (down) = Quadrant IV (bottom-right).
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant II needs a negative x-coordinate. This point's x is positive, so it sits on the right side of the plane.
In Quadrant III both coordinates are negative, but only the y-coordinate is negative here.
hints: Positive x pushes you RIGHT; negative y drops you DOWN.
Find the corner that is right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. Quadrants I–IV go counterclockwise from top-right.
Try a sample point like (3, -2): go right 3, then down 2. See which corner of the grid that lands in.
questions.stemEs: Un punto tiene la coordenada x positiva y la coordenada y negativa. ¿En qué cuadrante está?
questions.explanationEs: x positiva (derecha) y y negativa (abajo) = cuadrante IV (abajo a la derecha).
hintsEs: Una x positiva te lleva a la DERECHA; una y negativa te baja.
Halla la esquina que está a la derecha del eje y y debajo del eje x. Los cuadrantes I–IV van en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.
Prueba un punto de ejemplo como (3, −2): ve 3 a la derecha y luego 2 hacia abajo. Mira en qué esquina de la cuadrícula cae.

questions.stem: Which point is located on the x-axis?
questions.explanation: A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0. (4, 0) is on the x-axis.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is ___.
You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Neither coordinate is 0, so this point sits inside a quadrant rather than on an axis. A point on an axis has a coordinate of 0.
hints: A point ON the x-axis never moves up or down — its height is zero.
Check each pair's y-coordinate (the second number). On the x-axis, the y must be 0.
Read the second number in each pair. A point sits on the x-axis only when that number is 0.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál punto está ubicado sobre el eje x?
questions.explanationEs: Un punto está sobre el eje x cuando su coordenada y es 0. (4, 0) está sobre el eje x.
hintsEs: Un punto SOBRE el eje x nunca sube ni baja — su altura es cero.
Revisa la coordenada y (el segundo número) de cada par. En el eje x, la y debe ser 0.
Lee el segundo número de cada par. Un punto está sobre el eje x solo cuando ese número es 0.

reviewHighlights.formula: Quadrant I: (+, +) | Quadrant II: (−, +) | Quadrant III: (−, −) | Quadrant IV: (+, −)
steps: 3. Quadrant III: Lower-left (−, −); Quadrant IV: Lower-right (+, −)
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants is matching each sign to the wrong axis — for example, seeing (-2, 5) and thinking "the x is negative so I move DOWN, and the y is positive so I move RIGHT," which lands the point in Quadrant IV. But the x-coordinate always controls left/right, never up/down: negative x means LEFT (not down), and positive y means UP (not right). So (-2, 5) is actually left 2, up 5 — Quadrant II. Before you submit, check that you used the x-coordinate for left/right and the y-coordinate for up/down, and never swapped them.

choiceFeedback: Not quite. Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = ___.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Moving right changes ONLY the x-coordinate. The y-coordinate stays at 3.
Add the move to the x-value: take -5 and count up 8. Careful crossing zero — use a number line if it helps.

level3.prompt: A point starts in Quadrant I at (4, 6). Describe a move that puts it in Quadrant III. What must happen to both coordinates? Can you give the exact new coordinates after your move?
level3.sentenceFrame: To move from Quadrant I to Quadrant III, both coordinates must become ___. Starting at (4, 6), I could move ___ units left and ___ units down to reach (___,___), which is in Quadrant III because ___.
level3.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region — think about what must be true of BOTH signs there.
Plan moves that flip each sign: enough LEFT to push x = 4 below zero, enough DOWN to push y = 6 below zero.
Try moving left MORE than 4 units — say how far x = 4 travels and where it lands. Then plan the down move for y = 6.
level3.explanation: Quadrant III is the bottom-left region, so both coordinates have to end up negative. Starting at (4, 6), you need to move more than 4 units left to push x below 0 and more than 6 units down to push y below 0. Moving 6 left and 8 down, for example, lands on (-2, -2), which is Quadrant III because x and y are both negative.
level3.explanationEs: El Cuadrante III es la región inferior izquierda, así que las dos coordenadas deben terminar negativas. Empezando en (4, 6), necesitas moverte más de 4 unidades a la izquierda para llevar x por debajo de 0 y más de 6 unidades hacia abajo para llevar y por debajo de 0. Por ejemplo, moverte 6 a la izquierda y 8 hacia abajo cae en (-2, -2), que está en el Cuadrante III porque x y y son negativas.
level3.promptEs: Un punto empieza en el cuadrante I en (4, 6). Describe un movimiento que lo lleve al cuadrante III. ¿Qué debe pasar con las dos coordenadas? ¿Puedes dar las coordenadas nuevas exactas después de tu movimiento?
hintsEs: El Cuadrante III es la región de abajo a la izquierda: piensa qué debe cumplirse con AMBOS signos ahí.
Planea movimientos que cambien cada signo: suficiente IZQUIERDA para que x = 4 baje de cero y suficiente ABAJO para que y = 6 baje de cero.
Prueba moverte MÁS de 4 unidades a la izquierda: di cuánto viaja x = 4 y dónde cae. Luego planea el movimiento hacia abajo para y = 6.
